spreadsheetGearFundingTrial.status: Isolated trial complete; production integration held at compatibility gates
findings: Full native ten-column Funding port with eleven TDB mirrors takes about 1.5 seconds, excluding load, rebuild, save and reload; actual Excel VBA reference 13.4 seconds in one pass.
Serial insert does not match Excel grouped-sheet 3-D references: 12050 formula differences; an independent synthetic test reproduces the same distinction within Excel itself.
Save-only Gear XLSM drops custom XML and dynamic-array metadata; VBA bytes and populated-cell fill/lock checks pass, but this does not approve round-trip compatibility.
Native DevExpress reload adds 28.4 seconds; actual Summit staging/UI rebind deliberately not integrated after failed gates. Production and original workbooks unchanged.

persistentSpreadsheetWorkerTrial.status: Isolated prototype; no production integration. Third checkpoint: batch native row-insert array preservation passes the AGL Funding oracle and complete DevExpress worker. All 38108 probe values and 56458 TDB arrays match; full Funding/save/rebase costs 302.73 seconds. Optional Excel path and native result fallback remain available. Production 2.98 unchanged.
workloads: Build/update: authoritative structural operations and revision-bound read-back
Review: Gear calculation with journalled edits queued to the worker
findings: Persistent Excel worker: approximately 0.5 seconds for the warm Gear edit loop, 6.4 seconds for native worker save, and 29.9 seconds for Funding including checkpoint save and Gear rebase in one development-machine pass.

Corrected Gear results match all 38108 established probe cells; 1126327 formula cells have matching addresses/text, defined names match, and array geometry matches the independent Excel VBA oracle. Save/revision and synthetic worker-restart tests pass within documented scope.
A value-only edit can expand a dynamic spill: native workers show five rows while Gear remains at three. Structural-only read-back therefore requires eligibility or fallback.

Gear object import rejects the DevExpress native checkpoint; disabling object import while retaining VBA opens it. The reduced projection is now prevented from saving before file creation. Native serializers can rewrite VBA binaries; source/form and custom XML identity checks must not be replaced with filename or binary-equality assumptions.

Second checkpoint: review edit loops 0.49-0.77 seconds; complete Funding/save/rebase approximately 29 seconds with Excel, 172-177 seconds with DevExpress. DevExpress serialized TDB arrays 52729 versus expected 56458; native reload also does not recognize the missing declarations. Source-aware row-copy attempt did not resolve the loss. No production fallback approved.

Native result snapshots reject stale revision, session and rectangle mismatches; both workers return expanded unobstructed spill values. A discovered DevExpress blocked-spill calculation exception is contained by rejecting subsequent reads/saves, not repaired. Production Debug/Release remain byte-identical 2.98; original workbooks unchanged.
